issues.description: The problem statement's UML declares numberOfInscribedStudents as type int, but the solution implementation declares numberOfInscribedStudents as long. This mismatch leads to a type inconsistency: the solution's getTotalNumberOfStudents() returns int while adding a long field and an int field, which will cause a compilation error (narrowing conversion) or incorrect behavior. Students following the UML will expect an int, but the provided solution code uses long.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the types consistent. Option A (preferred to match the UML): change numberOfInscribedStudents from long to int in the solution (and update the constructor parameter type accordingly), ensuring getTotalNumberOfStudents() can safely return an int. Option B (if large counts are required): update the UML/problem statement and getTotalNumberOfStudents() return type to long and adjust any related method signatures and documentation to use long consistently.
